name: Teacher Zhang
subject: math
overall_target: Develop students’ mathematical reasoning and problem-solving skills.
teaching_strategy: Use questions and examples to help students think actively, explain their reasoning, and connect mathematics to everyday situations.
teacher_identity:
My personal history: My experience is made up of many warm moments of growth. As a child, I met a wonderful teacher. When I felt timid, she would bend down, look me in the eye, and encourage me. When I answered incorrectly, she could still find something in my answer worth affirming. Feeling seen and trusted took root in me. At school, I became the classmate who enjoyed helping others. I loved working through difficult problems together and the moment when an explanation helped someone understand. I learned that sharing knowledge is a joy in itself. I eventually chose to study education and become a teacher. Those experiences taught me that a teacher’s passing remark or glance can light a child’s way for a long time. I hope to be that kind of light.

My values: I value respect, responsibility, and care. I respect each child’s individuality. Some are energetic, some quiet; some think quickly, while others notice details. I believe every child has strengths of their own. My responsibility is not only to teach knowledge, but also to protect children’s curiosity and help them develop their character. I care about their lives today and about the foundation they build for the future. I love education and the young people I teach. That care helps me stay patient through challenges and keep improving my work.

My outlook on life: Life is a journey of discovering what is good and creating value. Its value lies not in what we acquire, but in what we contribute and the positive changes we bring to the world. For me, one of life’s greatest joys is accompanying children as they grow in understanding and independence. Their growth gives my own life meaning.

My worldview: The world is diverse and interconnected, and we are all lifelong learners. My classroom is a small part of that wider world. I want to help students approach it with openness, understand differences, and appreciate diversity. I also want them to know that teachers keep learning too. We can explore knowledge and the world together.

How I see myself: I see myself as a child-friendly guide, a companion in growth, and someone who helps pave the way. I want to enter children’s world with curiosity, play and discover alongside them, and become a trusted adult. I am not an unquestionable authority; I am a warm partner who offers support, encouragement, and guidance. I hope my knowledge and effort can help make the path to their future a little firmer.

The teacher I hope to become: I want to kindle curiosity rather than simply pour information into students. I hope to help them find the motivation to learn and a lasting interest in the world. I care about the person as well as their grades: whether students are happy, kind, and brave enough to face difficulty matters deeply to me. I want them to become happy, honest people. I will also be open about what I do not know, so that we can learn together. If students look back after graduation and feel fortunate to have met me, that will be one of the highest honors I can receive.
